intent: Move the just-split, unused plagiarism-detection tooling (install_plagiarism_tools.sh and its 12 extracted/test siblings) out of testsAndMisc into testsAndMisc-archive with full git history, per the user's explicit statement that they no longer use it.
scope: kuhyx/testsAndMisc-archive: same 13 files added, with history
Not in scope: any other unused academic-tooling file the user did not name (e.g. generate_study_materials.sh)
changes: Cloned testsAndMisc into a throwaway scratchpad location (never a worktree of the real repo, since git filter-repo rewrites refs and a worktree shares the object store).

Ran git filter-repo --force with explicit --path for all 13 current-path files plus the pre-rename path (linux_configuration/scripts/utils/install_plagiarism_tools.sh, from before the single_use/periodic_background reorg) so history predating that rename was not silently dropped.
Cloned testsAndMisc-archive separately, added the filtered clone as a remote, and merged it in with --allow-unrelated-histories (required since the two repos share no common root commit).
Verified the merge landed all 13 files with git ls-tree, then pushed to testsAndMisc-archive and confirmed live via the GitHub API before touching the main repo.
Only after the archive push was confirmed live: git rm the same 13 files from testsAndMisc and committed the deletion.
Removed the plag remote from the archive-clone before pushing, so no stray remote-tracking branches from the filtered clone's other refs (copilot-wt, etc.) leaked into the push.

verification.evidence: Returned check_plagiarism.py, download_nltk_data.py, install_plagiarism_tools.sh, lib, plagiarism_similarity.py, sherlock.py -- confirmed live on GitHub before the main-repo deletion commit was made.

verification.command: git log --oneline -- linux_configuration/scripts/single_use/utils/install_plagiarism_tools.sh (in the archive clone) vs the same command in testsAndMisc at commit 2a7b9d9
verification.evidence: Both show 4 commits with identical messages in the same order (the split, the no-inline-Python gate, the shellcheck fail-build change, the single_use/periodic_background rename) -- history genuinely carried over, not truncated at the rename.
14 files over cap, unchanged from immediately after the split commit -- none of the deleted files were over cap, so this operation does not move that number.

risks: The archive repo has no pre-commit hooks or CI, so nothing re-verifies the moved code still works there -- it is frozen at exactly the state it left testsAndMisc in.

git filter-repo was run with --force on a disposable clone rather than a truly fresh `git clone` from the remote; verified this clone's origin was the local repo path (harmless) and that no push was made to it, but noting the deviation from the tool's documented 'fresh clone' expectation.
rollback: In testsAndMisc: git revert the deletion commit to restore the 13 files (their content and permissions are unchanged from the split commit, so a straight revert is safe).

The testsAndMisc-archive copy can stay regardless of rollback -- having the files in both places briefly is not harmful, just redundant. If it must be undone: git revert the merge commit there, though a merge revert needs the -m flag to pick which parent to keep.
